coverage: Covering roughly Nov 8–9, 2026. Compiled Monday morning, ET.

items.headline: Nvidia’s board opens an independent probe into Jensen Huang; the stock slides premarket
items.summary: Huang told employees he had been unfaithful to his wife, after reporting tied him to a businesswoman US authorities reportedly concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia’s board said it has “no reason to believe” national security or company secrets were compromised and put independent directors and outside counsel in charge of an investigation; Huang said he will cooperate fully. @GavinSBaker, who has known him for almost 30 years, said he does not believe Huang would knowingly hurt America or Nvidia. China called the allegations “groundless speculation and slander,” and @KobeissiLetter reported NVDA down more than 5% as premarket trading opened.
items.short: Huang admits affair; board probes spy claims; China denies; NVDA down 5% premarket.

items.headline: US data center construction spending up 90% a year, a record $96.5B rate
items.summary: September data center construction ran at a record annualized $96.5 billion, up 90% from a year earlier and the biggest jump in ten years, @KobeissiLetter reported; it has nearly quadrupled since the start of 2024. Office construction fell 8% to $46.0 billion, near its lowest since 2016. Separately, @jukan05 relayed a Nikkei report that Musk’s Terafab told equipment suppliers it is targeting 1 million wafers a month from 2032, 700,000 of them for memory.
items.short: Data center builds +90% YoY to $96.5B; Terafab targets 1M wafers/month by 2032.

items.headline: Musk: the Cybertruck line shuts in about eight months to make room for Cybercab
items.summary: Elon Musk said Cybertruck orders far exceed production, and Tesla will build as many as it can before shutting the line in about eight months, returning many deposits. He said the truck is not unprofitable; the complexity simply costs more than the extra Cybercab output it would free up.
items.short: Cybertruck line ends in ~8 months; capacity goes to Cybercab.

Dumb Down version of $CRWV and $NVDA GPU ABS problem.

CoreWeave has a DDTL for project backed by $NVDA GPUs. The amount they can draw during buildout is about 50% of the true cost and 35% of what their true OpEx is. That means $CRWV needs to raise roughly 3x the amount of money outside the DDTL to meet contract terms on timed expansion. items.author: The Kobeissi Letter
items.text:
You can't make this up:

At 6:00 PM ET, US stock market futures opened for the first time since Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to a "relationship" with a Chinese spy.

By 6:01 PM ET, S&P 500 futures had erased an implied -$300 billion in market cap.

Then, by 6:07 PM ET, all losses were erased and S&P 500 futures turned green, adding back an implied +$350 billion in market cap as traders bought the dip.

That's a $650 billion swing in implied market cap due to a CEO's relationship.

We all just witnessed the strangest record in stock market history.

items.author: Alexandr Wang
items.text:
i forgot about this until @ScottWu46 reminded me, but back in january 2017 when we were 19, scott and i had lunch in SF

at lunch, we talked about how our IMO/IOI/math competition gang could be the next paypal mafia. i knew the competition kids were geniuses by any standard, and felt confident in time we could take the tech world by storm

fast forward nearly 10 years later, and many of our friends from that time are some of the most exciting people in AI and technology (@ScottWu46, @akshat_b, @chameleon_jeff, Jerry Ma, @randomjohnnyh, @0xShitTrader, @stevenkplus1, @thejessezhang, @vickie_ye_, @alexwei_, @demi_guo_, @d_m_ziegler, @hughbzhang, @_mohansolo, @MarkSellke, and many others i'm sure i'm forgetting)

i'm now at that age where i reminisce about everyone i grew up with, and i've known most of these people since middle school (via MATHCOUNTS!). even though we were scattered around the country, we would gchat about math problems and hang out on AoPS, then we did math/algo camps together, and then we did internships together.

very crazy to think about the degree of sheer brilliance of this group when we were just teenagers, and so special to see so many go on to leave their mark on the world.

note to parents: if your kid is on gchat all day solving math problems with some anonymous group of cross-country asian kids, (s)he may just turn out alright.

items.author: Riva
items.text:
Many people in tech have made, or are about to make, large sums of capital. I want to make a petition for more philanthropy towards historical buildings- specifically Churches 

Every year, dozens of historical Churches fall into disrepair around Europe. Hundreds of these deconsecrated buildings are up for sale

I don't believe you need to be Christian to recognise the value in saving these buildings. You just have to respect history. It is a travesty to see these buildings- that were the cradle of communities and our civilisation- fall into disrepair or even get demolished

These Churches should not become financial assets- not yoga studios, not backdrops for light shows, not a rental opportunity. We should allow them to remain as sacred spaces- the preservation of our history is enough 

When you take on these sorts of projects, people will say, "Oh, but these are money drains! They will just need continuous repair- and you'll have nobody to sell them to!" Consider perhaps that in this you will find the whole point 

You could save a Church for low six figures. A very wealthy person could save a lot of them. I have taken on one, and it has been one of the most beautiful and meaningful projects of my life

items.author: Serenity
items.text:
Various commentary from Qualcomm, Arm, to Meta executives this week during the AI selloff: 

$LITE CEO: "You had a comment from the CEO of $IREN and I'd second that. There's a massive disconnect in what we're seeing in our demand books. 

And what the markets are showing. And yet you're seeing a massive, massive selloff." (Fri, Nov 6)

$AMD CEO CNBC: "We're at the very beginning of the adoption cycle, where people can see where AI and superintelligence will take us" 

"We are seeing demand being higher than supply" (Wed, Nov 4)

$ARM CEO regarding a debate whether AI infrastructure spending is about to peak:

"I think in some states where it gets harder, other states may pick it up to make it easier, but I do believe strongly that if the US hesitates in any way shape performance in terms of data center buildout...

"The rest of the world is ready and willing. There is just huge demand for this capacity. And I think globally the US really wants to be able to compete against China. China is not slowing down at all." (Thu, Nov 5)

$APLD CEO: Bank construction lending, project financing and bond markets remain available, although interest rates and credit spreads have risen

"The big risk is delivering on time." "The demand picture is extremely robust." (Mon, Nov 2)

$QCOM CEO: "It's not demand bound. It's a supply bound." 

"We're short on wafers, we're short on substrate, we're short on assembly. Everything is short because demand is very, very high." 

"I think what the market is reacting to is what is the speed of the compute build out."

$META on political risk: "We did have a governor that won last night who did make data centers a big part of the platform.

Say as soon as we get past the inauguration, let's meet because we don't want to lose this investment in our town. We don't want these jobs to go elsewhere." (Wed, Nov 4)

Even politicians campaigning against data centers are negotiating. But Meta's president also emphasized that starting new US DCs will become more difficult. 

TLDR:
-> Extremely bullish commentary from accelerator players, networking, and semi companies
-> DC developers report strong pricing/demand, but increasingly emphasize financing, permitting and execution risks (more cautious)
-> Politicians that previously campaigned against DCs are showing cooperation

There's an important difference between demand disappearing and demand being delayed by the inability to build fast enough.

Despite the severity of the selloff, I'm not seeing evidence of widespread AI demand destruction in commentary.

items.author: Daniel Koss
items.text:
Like everyone else, I can't stop thinking about the Jensen news. It matters to me on two levels.

Professionally:

It does appear that $NVDA's criticisms around China entanglement were not completely made up. But instead of speculating, let's wait for the investigation and the facts. Most speculation on X is just people seeing what they want to be true.

A divorce, and his wife selling $NVDA shares, could create a new type of seller in the short term. It doesn't change the fundamentals or the AI trade.

Jensen having to step down, or worse, would be a different story. He isn't just a visionary. He IS NVIDIA. That would hurt $NVDA, which is the backbone of AI today.

Personally:

Jensen is maybe my favorite founder of all time. Part of his charm was one company and one wife, loyal from the start. He always spoke about her in the highest terms, never cursed, stayed positive, and seemed like the highest-integrity guy in tech.

What he does in his private life is none of my business. I don't have the details or the context.

I'm just deeply sad to hear this story.

items.headline: One iron infusion lifted fitness about 10% in a common type of heart failure
items.summary: In a 65-person Mass General Brigham trial presented at the American Heart Association meeting, a single 1,000 mg IV iron dose raised peak oxygen uptake about 10% at 12 weeks in iron-deficient patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; placebo was unchanged.
items.short: Single IV iron dose: ~10% better VO2 in HFpEF.

items.headline: A microbiome pill cut bloodstream infections after stem-cell transplants in an early trial
items.summary: In a phase 1 trial run by City of Hope, Memorial Sloan Kettering and Seres Therapeutics, the bacterial therapy SER-155 was well tolerated, and patients who got it had fewer bloodstream infections and lower levels of the harmful gut bacteria linked to them.
items.short: SER-155: fewer bloodstream infections in phase 1.

items.headline: Brain-activated CAR-T cells cleared an incurable childhood tumor in mice
items.summary: UCSF researchers engineered CAR-T cells, called B-SYNC, that stay inactive until they reach the brain. In two mouse models they completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma, a childhood brain cancer that is almost always fatal within a year. Human trials have not started.
items.short: UCSF B-SYNC CAR-T eliminated DMG in mice.

items.author: Mgoes
items.summary: A list of ten results from the past six months that mostly went unread in press releases: a pill that doubled median survival in metastatic pancreatic cancer, one-time gene edits that cut angioedema attacks and LDL cholesterol, a personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine that beat Keytruda alone, and a pig kidney that kept a man off dialysis for 271 days. His point: the body is turning into a software problem with a shrinking update cycle.

items.title: We are shooting our own foots with zoning laws
items.author: J.K. Lundblad
items.summary: Infrastructure in cities scales sublinearly with population (exponent about 0.85), while patents, GDP and incomes scale superlinearly (about 1.15). Bigger cities get more out of each person, so zoning that caps city size caps human potential.

items.summary: Millerd expects more opportunity, not less, for people who learn to work with agentic coding models, and says many people are reaching out to him about letting go of a fancy work identity. His advice: don’t trade your present for the future. Fear and the sense of being “behind” steal the present, which is the only place curiosity and creativity happen.

items.title: Four Cards
items.rule: If a day's forecast says rain, the card shows an umbrella on the back.
items.explanation: Rain could hide something that breaks the rule; Scarf breaks it if the other side turns out to be Rain. Umbrella can't break it (the rule never says only those cards have it), and Sunny isn't covered by the rule at all. Most people pick the card that matches the rule's second half instead of the one that could falsify it.

Samsung and Hyundai are about to talk robot memory at the very top.

According to Seoul Economic Daily, Samsung and Hyundai Motor Group are holding their first ever top management exchange on November 9, with about 170 executives meeting at Samsung's training center in Yongin.

Memory supply for Hyundai's Atlas humanoid robot is expected to be one of the big topics on the table.

Hyundai plans to mass produce 30,000 Atlas units a year in the United States starting in 2028. …
